title: Hunting is for Girls—at Least Among Bonobos - Nautilus
author: Jake Currie
text: Subscribe to skip adsAdvertisementZoologyHunting is for Girls—at Least Among BonobosThey out-hunt their male counterpartsJCBy Jake Currie1:00 PM CDT on October 28, 2026Add Nautilus to GoogleBonobos have a well-earned reputation as the hippies of the great apes. Not only do they practice free love, using sex to bond socially, the more matriarchal species are also generally more cooperative and less violent than their patriarchal chimpanzee relatives. These different evolutionary pathways were most likely carved by the Congo River around 1.5 to 2 million years ago and are rooted in their diets. Unlike bonobos, chimps north of the river shared their territory with gorillas and competed with them for fruit, forcing them to adopt an omnivorous diet that relied on hunting. Their close relatives south of the river lived in a gorilla-free territory, allowing female bonobos to form social foraging groups that gathered fruit.
